body: No splits. First listed week Mar 2007 ₹272 → ATH ₹53,453 (Oct 2022) ≈197x; ₹31,065 on 19 Nov 2026 (−42% from ATH). Twin engine: P/E 26.6 → 81.4 (3.1x) × implied EPS ~64x (TTM EPS ₹14.9 → ₹657); the business did most of the work. Drawdowns: −41% (2008), −38% (2015–16), −52% (Aug 2018–Apr 2020). Early signal: exclusive Jockey licensee for India since 1994 (renewed to 2030); revenue CAGR ~35% FY04–15 with a new product line almost every year; ROCE 50–70% with negligible debt; P/E fell to ~13 at end-2008, so a fast grower was briefly priced like a commodity company. Investors who caught it (2008–2010) mostly just held. Ended/stalled: after the 2022 peak, FY23 trade destocking and weak demand cut TTM EPS from ₹658 to ₹458; EPS recovered to ₹708 by 2026 (above 2022), but P/E fell from ~81 to ~44, so 4 years of EPS growth were erased by de-rating. Sales CAGR slowed to ~11% (FY15–26). Lesson: brand-licence compounders bought at 13–30x make money; at 80x+ the next four years depend entirely on growth not slowing. Licence concentration (Jockey International) is a permanent tail risk.

data.early_signals: exclusive licence, 60%+ ROCE, P/E ~13 in 2008, new categories yearly
data.lesson: de-rating can erase years of EPS growth
data.note: Prices: screener.in weekly closes, split/bonus-adjusted. P/E = trailing (TTM) from screener chart; 'implied EPS x' = price multiple / P/E multiple.

title: Page Industries 2007–2022: Jockey licence compounder, ~197x, then de-rating

body: THE GOOD NUMBER: Gitanjali Gems reported large revenues and profits, ran well-known jewellery brands, and its bank loans were 'standard' with regular debt servicing until Dec 2017; over 30 lenders (SBI, StanChart, BoI, BoB...) were exposed per the FY17 annual report. WHY IT LIED: a large share of its business was with its own group: group-company receivables were reported at ~33% of the company's total receivables, so 'sales' partly moved money within the promoter's network. Import trade was financed by letters of undertaking from PNB with credit of ~360 days against RBI's 90-day norm for precious-stone imports; PNB later found 151 fraudulent LoUs and no proof the trades were bona fide. Feb 2018: PNB declared the fraud (Nirav Modi/Mehul Choksi); Gitanjali fell ~61% in seven days. TELLS THAT WERE PUBLIC OR SEMI-PUBLIC: SMA-2 classification in 2014 after >60-day payment delays; a March 2017 auditor warning of default to LIC; a sharp fall in promoter Mehul Choksi's shareholding; sector receivables at ~5 months of sales (CARE). TEST: related-party share of receivables and sales; receivable days vs domestic peers; whether credit periods exceed regulatory norms; promoter stake trend. LESSON: receivables owed by your own group are not assets; pre-2018 debtor-days data was not found this session [gap].

data.good_number: large reported revenue and profits, a big branded jewellery network, loans serviced and classified 'standard' until Dec 2017, 30+ lending banks
data.test_that_catches_it: related-party share of receivables; credit period vs regulation/industry; SMA-2 history; promoter stake trend; number of lenders
data.why_misleading: receivables were concentrated in group companies (~33% of total receivables) and trade was financed by fraudulent PNB letters of undertaking with ~360-day credit vs a 90-day norm

title: Hidden trap: Gitanjali Gems' revenue and 'standard' loans
